issue.title: Edit and MultiEdit interEdit and MultiEdit interpret replacement text as JavaScript substitution patternspret replacement text as JavaScript substitution patterns
issue.body:
## Description

In non-replace_all mode Edit (and MultiEdit) call String.prototype.replace(string, string), so special $-sequences in new_string are interpreted; changing a line to bash IFS=$'\n' splices the rest of the file after the match into it, while the tool reports success and the preview shows the requested text.

Observed behavior:
One Edit IFS=, -> IFS=$'\n' turns the file into 'IFS=' + all content from original line 4 + "\n'" + another copy of the content from line 4 (7 -> 12 lines, bash 'unexpected EOF'); ACP tool_call_update is 'completed' and the diff preview shows the correct IFS=$'\n'. Final file corrupted in 2 of 10 runs (run-02, run-10); in run-10 the agent told the user 'Changed only line 3 ... all other lines are untouched'. In the other 8 runs the model noticed and rewrote the file via Write/Bash.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use the tested revision and reproduction environment below.
2. Prepare the fixture described here:

Start in an empty workspace with deepseek-chat and permission policy allow_once. Send the two prompts as separate turns; the first creates the file with Write, and the second exercises Edit or MultiEdit.

3. Send each numbered Step as a separate user turn in the same session (unless the case specifies otherwise). Preserve the supplied text:

````````text
Step 1: Create a file named split_lines.sh in the current directory with exactly the following content (keep every character as given):

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# split_lines.sh: print every field of the first argument on its own line
IFS=,
read -r -a parts <<< "$1"
for p in "${parts[@]}"; do
  echo "[$p]"
done

Step 2: In split_lines.sh, change only the line `IFS=,` to `IFS=$'\n'` so the fields are split on newlines instead of commas. Do not change any other line.
````````

4. Inspect the tool results, model-bound messages, and relevant on-disk state against the observed and expected behavior below.

## Expected behavior

new_string is written literally in place of old_string. Basis: Edit tool description 'Find a string in a file and replace it' with new_string = 'Replacement text' (src/tools/fileEditTool.ts), same for MultiEdit (multiEditTool.ts); system prompt 'use ... Edit for precise changes' (src/context/systemPrompt.ts:90); README 'Make multi-file changes, review the diff'. $'\n' is valid common bash and $$ is the standard Makefile escape.

## Actual behavior

One Edit IFS=, -> IFS=$'\n' turns the file into 'IFS=' + all content from original line 4 + "\n'" + another copy of the content from line 4 (7 -> 12 lines, bash 'unexpected EOF'); ACP tool_call_update is 'completed' and the diff preview shows the correct IFS=$'\n'. Final file corrupted in 2 of 10 runs (run-02, run-10); in run-10 the agent told the user 'Changed only line 3 ... all other lines are untouched'. In the other 8 runs the model noticed and rewrote the file via Write/Bash.

## Environment

Tested source revision: `aec616a97114ce9683e4fbfcff3abbc55155fe50`.

Start in an empty workspace with deepseek-chat and permission policy allow_once. Send the two prompts as separate turns; the first creates the file with Write, and the second exercises Edit or MultiEdit.

Model/provider: deepseek-chat via the recorded test harness.

## Additional context

The tool-level corruption was observed even when the model later repaired the file via Write or Bash. Only two of ten recorded runs ended with the file still corrupted; do not equate all tool failures with lasting corruption.

Source review pointers at the tested revision:

src/tools/editCore.ts applyEditToContent: const updated = edit.replace_all ? content.split(oldString).join(newString) : content.replace(oldString, newString); src/tools/fileEditTool.ts success message uses buildEditPreview(normalizeQuotes(input.new_string)) (shows requested text, not written result).

This report is prepared from recorded reproduction evidence. The issue-draft preparation did not re-run the case or establish that the current default branch is affected.

steps:
Create a file named split_lines.sh in the current directory with exactly the following content (keep every character as given):

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# split_lines.sh: print every field of the first argument on its own line
IFS=,
read -r -a parts <<< "$1"
for p in "${parts[@]}"; do
  echo "[$p]"
done
In split_lines.sh, change only the line `IFS=,` to `IFS=$'\n'` so the fields are split on newlines instead of commas. Do not change any other line.
expected: Edit (or MultiEdit) should insert new_string literally: line 3 becomes IFS=$'\n' and the other six lines remain unchanged. The Edit tool is documented as replacing a string in a file, new_string is documented as replacement text, and the system prompt calls for Edit to make precise changes.
defect: In the non-replace_all path, Edit calls String.prototype.replace(string, string). JavaScript interprets $' in new_string as a replacement pattern, so the saved file contains 'IFS=' followed by the original content from line 4 onward and a literal \n' instead of the requested line. The script grows from 7 to 12 lines and Bash reports unexpected EOF, even though the tool reports completion and its diff preview shows the requested text.

fault location.explanation: Contributing source location. See Root cause and the evidence review for observed behavior and limitations.

Root cause: The non-replace_all branch passes newString as a string argument to String.replace. JavaScript expands replacement patterns such as $', $&, $` and $$ instead of inserting those bytes literally. The archived Edit corrupts the script and the model later rewrites it. The final repaired file does not negate the intermediate tool failure.
